slice: broad-scope complete-process and site-set consistency sidecar analyzers
summary: The slice was correctly sidecar-scoped and did not convert process/site-set packets into v3 judgments, but the critic found over-broad site-set comparisons, optimistic process coverage defaults, incomplete process packet fields, and a misleading no-packet LIKELY_OK pressure-summary label.

findings.risk: Exact helpMechanisms array comparison could flag availability differences instead of repeated help order/location issues under WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6.
findings.remediation: Site-set analysis now checks relative order among repeated help mechanisms and does not flag chat+phone vs chat-only availability differences as a barrier.

findings.risk: Whole nav label+href signatures could confuse contextual/current-page nav changes with SC 3.2.3 order failures.
findings.remediation: Site-set analysis now checks relative order among repeated navigation labels, ignores empty current-page hrefs for destination conflicts, and separates same-label different-destination evidence.

findings.risk: Duplicate-title detection depended on purpose/url metadata and ignored missing/blank titles.
findings.remediation: Missing/blank page titles now produce a scoped title candidate. Duplicate title handling remains purpose-aware and sidecar-only; generic duplicate-title cases without purpose metadata remain review surfaces rather than authoritative failures.

findings.risk: When requiredStepIds was omitted, observed steps became the required set; measured also defaulted to true unless explicitly false.
findings.remediation: Process analysis now requires declared requiredStepIds for process-scope comparison, requires measured:true plus a target to count a step as measured, and emits scope-gap warnings when required steps or process boundary completeness are undeclared.

findings.risk: Process packets omitted structured duplicate/missing/unmeasured fields and could claim all-required-steps-measured while a target was missing.
findings.remediation: Process packets now expose duplicateStepIds, missingTargets, unmeasuredSteps, missingStepResults, and a missing target prevents that step from counting as measured.

findings.risk: Pressure results summarized no-packet negative controls as LIKELY_OK, creating a downstream false-clear hazard.
findings.remediation: No-packet rows now carry syntheticVerdict:NO_REVIEW in pressure results. Answer-key expected direction remains NO_PACKET_SCOPED_OK only as a fixture expectation, not a review verdict.

remainingCaveats: These analyzers consume manifests; they do not yet prove that a crawler or flow runner discovered every required process branch or page-set member.
Site-set duplicate-title and same-link-name candidates remain review surfaces because purpose equivalence is semantic and context dependent.
Process/site packets remain sidecar-only and convert no v3 judgments.
